chunks: Say: 'Call on those you imagine are gods apart from God. They are not masters even of an atom's weight in the heavens and the earth, nor do they have a share in them, nor is any one of them a helper (of God).'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the power of false gods compared to God?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah Saba, this verse serves as a decisive refutation of polytheism by exposing the ontological weakness of idols, which possess neither independent agency nor divine support. Shia exegetes emphasize that the phrase 'nor have they any share in their governance' underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah, contrasting the impotence of created beings with the self-sufficient nature of the Creator. This argument reinforces the concept of Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah, urging believers to direct worship solely to God who controls the minutest details of the universe.
